A raid is a crowd of new accounts joining a chat within moments, usually to flood it. With antiraid on, I count the joins: when too many come in a short time, the chat is in a raid for a while, and everybody who joins during it is dealt with, as are the people who made it a raid.

Some chats get a lot of users joining just to spam. They may be trolls, or part of a spam network.

To slow them down, turn captchas on. Everybody who joins is muted and has to pass a test to prove they're a real person before they can speak.

Captchas ride on the welcome message, so they only work while welcome messages are on (/welcome). With welcomes off nobody is muted.

Test types (/captchamode): button (press a button), math (pick the answer to a small sum), text (the code is written in the message; press the scrambled characters in the order of the code) and text2 (the same, but the code is a picture).

How it looks: the newcomer's welcome carries a verify button, the same for everybody. In button mode one press unmutes them; the other modes (and button mode with /captcharules) open a private chat with me where they solve the test. Somebody who is already verified only gets a small pop-up saying so.

If the chat uses join requests, the captcha is sent privately and the request is approved once it is solved.

Time: /captchamutetime unmutes people who haven't solved it after a while (by default they stay muted until they do). /captchakick removes people who run out of time (/captchakicktime). When both are set, the kick comes first.

Examples:
• Turn captchas on: /captcha on
• Use the math test: /captchamode math
• Make people accept the rules too: /captcharules on
• Unmute after a day even if unsolved: /captchamutetime 1d
• Stay muted until solved: /captchamutetime off

Chats can switch off what they don't need, in three ways.

/disable switches off single commands for members. /restrictmodule does the same for every command of a module. Admins can still use what is switched off for members, so nobody is locked out of their own tools. Aliases go with the command.

/disablemodule turns a whole module off in the chat completely: its commands stop for everybody, admins included, and so does everything it does by itself (filters, locks, flood control, welcome messages ...). Everything can go except this page: even /help and /connect. Turning connections off ends the ones that exist. /disablemodule all turns off everything but this page; a chat that only wants global bans sends it and then /enablemodule gbans. /enablemodule brings modules back. These two are for the chat's owner.

Only the commands on this page can never be switched off, so a chat can always undo what it did.

Some chats get a lot o' users joining just to spam. They may be trolls, or part o' a spam network.

To slow 'em down, turn captchas on. All hands who joins be muted an' has to pass a test to prove they're a real soul afore they can speak.

Captchas ride on the welcome aboard missive, so they only work while welcome aboard missives be on (/welcome). Wit' welcomes off nobody be muted.

Test types (/captchamode): button (press a button), math (pick the answer to a small sum), text (the code be written in the missive; press the scrambled characters in the order o' the code) an' text2 (the same, but the code be a picture).

How it looks: the newcomer's welcome aboard carries a verify button, the same fer all hands. In button mode one press unmutes 'em; the other modes (an' button mode wit' /captcharules) open a private chat wit' me where they solve the test. Some soul who be already verified only gets a small pop-up saying so.

If the chat uses join requests, the captcha be sent privately an' the request be approved once it be solved.

Time: /captchamutetime unmutes folk who haven't solved it after a while (by default they stay muted until they do). /captchakick removes folk who run out o' time (/captchakicktime). When both be set, the kick comes first.

Examples:
• Turn captchas on: /captcha on
• Use the math test: /captchamode math
• Make folk accept the rules too: /captcharules on
• Unmute after a day even if unsolved: /captchamutetime 1d
• Stay muted until solved: /captchamutetime off

• Wymuś też akceptację regulaminu: /captcharules on
• Odcisz po dobie, nawet jeśli nierozwiązana: /captchamutetime 1d
